sections.title: Sector Context
sections.content: All five semiconductor leaders closed lower in the latest session, with declines ranging from -2.32% (TSM) to -5.84% (INTC). The drop followed Broadcom earnings-related sector pressure even as Tier-1 analyst consensus remains Buy on four of five names. Long-term uptrends remain intact — every ticker trades above its 200-day SMA by 3% to 71% — though four of five are testing below their 50-day SMA, flagging near-term weakness. TSM's beta of 1.25 makes it the most defensive name in the cohort, while AMD's 2.47 beta explains both its 70%+ premium to SMA-200 and its -5.33% drawdown on the day.

data.title: Sector pullback tests support rather than invalidates the trend
data.evidence: All five tickers fell between -2.32% and -5.84% on the day, yet every name still trades above its 200-day SMA by 3% to 71%. The trigger was Broadcom earnings, per Yahoo Finance UK — not a structural breakdown. AMD's price sits 1.6% above SMA-50 while the rest are 1-17.5% below, suggesting the cohort is stretching supports rather than reversing long-term uptrends.

data.title: AVGO carries the cleanest valuation in the peer set
data.evidence: AVGO's 20.8x forward P/E is the cohort's lowest, its 0.44 PEG is the only sub-0.5 reading, and its $524.51 target implies +40% upside. The MACD (-3.59) sits above its signal line (-5.52) even after today's -5.03% drop, hinting at recovering momentum. Risk: the +40% upside assumes AVGO sustains its AI/custom-silicon trajectory.

data.title: INTC is the outlier — negative earnings against a 117x forward P/E
data.evidence: INTC is the only name with negative trailing EPS (-$0.60), a Hold consensus, and the highest forward P/E in the group (117.7x) — pricing in a recovery not yet visible in the data. The technicals match this uncertainty: RSI at 32.8 sits closest to oversold and price is 17.5% below the 50-day SMA, the deepest pullback in the cohort. Failure to deliver the implied earnings rebound would compound the multiple compression risk.

data.title: NVDA shows the only clean MACD bullish crossover in the group
data.evidence: Despite the sector-wide decline, NVDA's MACD (+0.17) crossed above its signal line (-1.77) and RSI at 63.8 sits elevated but neutral. The $301.62 target implies +45% upside, the largest in the peer set. This combination of positive MACD bias and largest analyst upside — while price sits only 1.1% below SMA-50 — is unusual during a 2.4% down day.

data.title: TSM is the structural defensive pick
data.evidence: TSM carries the lowest beta in the cohort (1.25) and declined the least today (-2.32%). The $250B US investment headline (Crypto Briefing, 0.494 Bullish score) layers onto a $498.24 analyst target (+21.6% upside) and 28% EPS growth projections (Foreign Policy Journal, 0.838 score). The trade-off: TSM sits right at its lower Bollinger Band ($409.21) and below SMA-50, flagging short-term support risk.

data.title: AMD and TSM carry the highest growth premiums relative to upside
data.evidence: AMD's 178.5x trailing P/E and 75.8x forward P/E, paired with TSM's 1.32 PEG (highest in group), sit alongside the two narrowest upsides to target (+4.9% AMD, +21.6% TSM). By contrast, AVGO and NVDA combine reasonable forward multiples with +40% to +45% upside, leaving AMD and TSM more exposed to negative earnings revisions during the current pullback.
